headline: Benchmarking predicted structures and design models against physical failure modes
label: Structure Prediction Validation Applications
summary: Predicted structures and design models are now judged against physical and experimental criteria rather than accepted at face value.
synthesis: The dominant thread is using computational models to design or diagnose protein binders, with outputs checked against criteria beyond the raw prediction. In the de novo SARS-CoV-2 RBD study, AlphaFold, molecular dynamics, docking and SAP signatures are combined to diagnose trade-offs between target binding and self-association, identifying failure modes in designed binders. An antigen-specific protein language model is applied to guide CDR optimization for antibody design, and a preprint reports Claude-enabled agentic antibody design yielding biparatopic IgE disruptors, three variants of which outperform omalizumab at removing bound IgE. What is new is the emphasis on diagnosing why designs fail, rather than accepting predicted structures or sequences at face value.
